result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_eulerian()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph has an Eulerian circuit. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L31781-L31841){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_eulerian() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is Eulerian](/assets/graphs/is-eulerian.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: a bowtie of two triangles sharing node C; badges give each node's degree and all are even, so a closed trail can use every edge once and is_eulerian() returns True. Right: the same bowtie plus an edge between B and E, which makes B and E odd (degree 3, shown in the accent color), so is_eulerian() returns False." width="100%"} An Eulerian circuit is a closed trail that visits every edge exactly once. For undirected graphs, an Eulerian circuit exists if and only if: - the graph is connected (ignoring isolated nodes) - all vertices have even degree For directed graphs, an Eulerian circuit exists if and only if: - the graph is weakly connected - every vertex has equal in-degree and out-degree ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph has an Eulerian circuit, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A cycle graph has an Eulerian circuit because every node has even degree (exactly 2): ::: {#18287e59 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(5) # Returns True (all degrees are 2) graph.is_eulerian() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: A path graph fails the test, since its two endpoints have odd degree (1): ::: {#03a0863d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(5) # Returns False (endpoints have odd degree) graph.is_eulerian() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: For directed graphs, the requirement is that in-degree equals out-degree at every node, which a directed cycle naturally satisfies: ::: {#af044213 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_cycle_graph(4) # Returns True (in-degree = out-degree for all) graph.is_eulerian() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
